name: bsky-copilot-mcp

tools.name: list_accounts
tools.description: Bluesky accounts configured on this machine, and which one is selected. Never returns API keys.

tools.name: switch_account
tools.description: Change which configured Bluesky account every other tool acts on. Say which account you switched to, so the user can see it.

handle.description: Handle of a configured account, e.g. alice.bsky.social

tools.name: get_account
tools.description:
Every account this key can post to. Bluesky and Threads, more than one of either, with the id each is addressed by, plus the timezone, plan features, groups, and whether an AI key is configured. Call this first if unsure. Read `key.group` to see whether this key is scoped to one group -- if so, that is the whole world this server can see, not a filtered view of a bigger one; an account outside it simply does not appear here. Read `default_group` to know where a post lands when no destination is named, and say that to the user rather than letting them find out after. Also refreshes the account’s notices, anything waiting on the user, such as scheduled posts that were never published.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

tools.name: get_performance_summary
tools.description:
Best and worst performing posts, total likes and post count. Free.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

tools.name: get_best_time_to_post
tools.description:
Ranked posting slots for this account, best first, bucketed in its own timezone. Free.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

weeks.description: How far back to look. Default 1.

tools.name: list_posts
tools.description:
This account’s stored post history with engagement figures. Free.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

tools.name: get_insights
tools.description:
Stored analysis of this account’s voice, topics and tone. Free, and never generates, returns empty if nothing has been analysed yet.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

tools.name: get_growth
tools.description:
Follower, following, post and like growth over time for this account. Free. Empty until at least two snapshots exist, sync_posts records one.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

tools.name: sync_posts
tools.description:
Refresh the stored post history from Bluesky. Call before analytics if you need up-to-the-minute numbers. Free, but makes outbound calls. For an account that posts less than weekly, pass depth: "full", force alone only bypasses the cache, it does not page further back.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

depth.description: recent (default) prefers the last week; full pages back to the 200-post limit.

tools.name: list_live_posts
tools.description:
Read posts straight from Bluesky, past the 200-post storage limit. Nothing is stored. Use when the user asks about a period older than the stored history covers. Follow next_cursor to page further back.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

tools.name: get_suggestion_prompt
tools.description:
PREFER THIS over generate_suggestions. Returns the exact prompt Bluesky Copilot would send, with this account’s real posts already interpolated. You are an LLM, run it yourself and write the results back with create_draft. Costs the user nothing and needs no AI key.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

topic.description: Optional subject to steer the ideas.

context.description: Ground truth the model must draw on: what actually shipped, real numbers, real dates. Without it, anything the topic implies but the account’s post history does not contain gets invented and stated as fact. Pass whatever the user has told you.

tools.name: get_rewrite_prompt
tools.description:
PREFER THIS over rewrite_post. Returns the exact rewrite prompt for you to run yourself. Costs the user nothing and needs no AI key.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

context.description: Ground truth the model must draw on: what actually shipped, real numbers, real dates. Without it, anything the topic implies but the account’s post history does not contain gets invented and stated as fact. Pass whatever the user has told you.

tools.name: generate_suggestions
tools.description:
Ask Kunopilot to generate post ideas. THIS COSTS THE USER MONEY. If they have their own Anthropic or OpenAI key configured it spends their provider credit; if they do not, it runs on Kunopilot’s key and spends 4 Kunopilot credits, and the reply reports `credits_charged`. **Always tell the user how many credits it cost.** If they cannot afford it the call is refused with `insufficient_credits` and a shortfall, do not retry, tell them the number. Only use when the user explicitly asks Kunopilot to do the generating, otherwise use get_suggestion_prompt, which is free and which you can run yourself.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

context.description: Ground truth the model must draw on: what actually shipped, real numbers, real dates. Without it, anything the topic implies but the account’s post history does not contain gets invented and stated as fact. Pass whatever the user has told you.

tools.name: rewrite_post
tools.description:
Ask Kunopilot to rewrite a draft. THIS COSTS THE USER MONEY. With their own API key configured it spends their provider credit; without one it runs on Kunopilot’s key for 1 Kunopilot credit, and the reply reports `credits_charged`. **Always tell the user how many credits it cost.** An empty balance is refused with `insufficient_credits`, do not retry. Prefer get_rewrite_prompt, which is free and which you can run yourself.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

context.description: Ground truth the model must draw on: what actually shipped, real numbers, real dates. Without it, anything the topic implies but the account’s post history does not contain gets invented and stated as fact. Pass whatever the user has told you.

tools.name: list_suggestions
tools.description:
Post ideas already stored for this account. Free.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

tools.name: delete_suggestion
tools.description:
Discard a stored suggestion.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

tools.name: list_drafts
tools.description:
Unpublished drafts for this account.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

tools.name: create_draft
tools.description:
Save a draft. One post, or several to make a thread in order. Nothing is published, this is the safe way to hand work back to the user.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

posts.description: One entry per post in the thread.

tools.name: reply_to_draft
tools.description:
Add one or more replies to a draft that already exists, turning it into a thread (or extending one). APPENDS TO THE END OF THE THREAD the target belongs to, not directly after the draft you name, because a Bluesky thread is a line. Use this instead of deleting and recreating: that would throw away the draft ids, tags, images and created_at. Note that update_draft cannot re-parent a draft; this is the only way to change thread structure after creation.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

id.description: The draft to reply to. Any member of the thread will do.

posts.description: One entry per reply, in order.

after.description: Insert after this draft instead of at the end. Must be in the same thread.

tools.name: export_drafts
tools.description:
Export drafts as CSV or JSON text. Returns {filename, content}, write content to filename, or show it to the user. Omit ids for every draft. Read the warnings array: it says when ids were skipped.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

tools.name: get_schedule_prompt
tools.description:
FREE. Returns a prompt that proposes when to post a set of drafts, using the account’s saved cadence and its own best-performing slots. You are an LLM, run it yourself, SHOW THE USER THE PROPOSED TIMES AND WAIT FOR THEM TO AGREE, then apply it with one schedule_draft call per entry. Never schedule a batch without asking first.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

tools.name: update_draft
tools.description:
Change a draft’s text or tags.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

tools.name: delete_draft
tools.description:
Delete a draft.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

tools.name: schedule_draft
tools.description:
Schedule an existing draft. Give scheduled_at in ISO 8601, ideally with an offset or Z, without one it is read in the account’s own timezone.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

account_ids.description: Which connected accounts to post to, by id from get_account. Omit to use the key’s own group if it has one, else the user’s default group. Use this OR group, never both. An id the key does not own -- or that exists but is outside the key’s group -- fails the whole call, nothing is silently dropped.

group.description: Post to a named group of accounts, e.g. "Business". Groups are listed by get_account. If this key is itself scoped to a group, that is the only name it can pass here. Use this OR account_ids, never both.

tools.name: publish_draft
tools.description:
PUBLISH A DRAFT TO BLUESKY NOW. Irreversible: it posts publicly and deletes the draft. Always ask the user before calling this, and only pass confirm: true once they have said yes. You must also pass confirm_handle naming the selected account, check it with get_account rather than guessing. This route posts to BLUESKY ONLY and takes no destinations: it predates multi-platform fan-out. To reach Threads or several accounts, schedule it with schedule_draft and account_ids instead.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

confirm.description: Must be true, and only after the user agrees.

confirm_handle.description: The handle of the selected account, named back as confirmation. Do not guess it.

tools.name: duplicate_draft
tools.description:
Copy an existing draft, including its tags.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

tools.name: list_scheduled
tools.description:
Posts already queued for this account. Statuses: pending (still to go out), posted, failed (Bluesky refused it), missed (never sent, it could not be published close enough to its scheduled time, usually an outage). A missed post is waiting on the user: offer to reschedule it with reschedule_post, post it as-is, or cancel it with cancel_scheduled.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

tools.name: schedule_posts
tools.description:
Queue a post or thread for a future time. Give scheduled_at in ISO 8601, ideally with an offset or Z, without one it is read in the account’s own timezone, which get_account reports. Name account_ids or group to choose destinations; doing so fixes them for good, so the post will not pick up an account connected later. The reply is `targets`, read it back to the user rather than assuming where it went.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

reply_to_uri.description: Make this a reply to an existing post: an at:// URI or a bsky.app link. Everything in `posts` shares one time, so this is the only way to answer something LATER, or to answer a post that was not scheduled by us. Get the URI from `uri` on a posted item in list_scheduled.

reply_to_scheduled_id.description: Reply to another of this account’s scheduled posts, which may not have published yet. Must be scheduled before this one. Use instead of reply_to_uri, not alongside it.

account_ids.description: Which connected accounts to post to, by id from get_account. Omit to use the key’s own group if it has one, else the user’s default group. Use this OR group, never both. An id the key does not own -- or that exists but is outside the key’s group -- fails the whole call, nothing is silently dropped.

group.description: Post to a named group of accounts, e.g. "Business". Groups are listed by get_account. If this key is itself scoped to a group, that is the only name it can pass here. Use this OR account_ids, never both.

tools.name: reschedule_post
tools.description:
Move a queued post. Moving any member of a thread moves the whole thread.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

tools.name: get_autopilot_config
tools.description:
How autopilot spaces a queue out: posts per day and the hour window.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

tools.name: set_autopilot_config
tools.description:
Change how autopilot spaces posts out. Hours are 0–23 in the account’s timezone.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

tools.name: queue_posts
tools.description:
Hand autopilot a batch of posts and let it pick the times. Send the whole batch in one call rather than one call per post, it lays the schedule out once. Falls back to the saved config for anything you omit.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

tools.name: cancel_scheduled
tools.description:
Remove a queued post. Cancelling a thread root cancels the whole thread. The credits it was holding are returned, and the reply says how many.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

tools.name: get_credits
tools.description:
The account’s credit balance, what is held against already-scheduled posts, and the full price list. Publishing spends credits; reading analytics does not. Check this before a large batch — a schedule that does not fit is refused whole, not truncated.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

tools.name: quote_credits
tools.description:
What a set of posts would cost, WITHOUT scheduling them. Call this before schedule_posts or queue_posts whenever the batch is more than a couple of posts, or whenever any of them contains a link — a link takes an X post from 6 credits to 40, because X charges us about thirteen times more for link posts. Writes nothing and holds nothing. If it does not fit, tell the user the shortfall rather than trying the schedule and reporting the failure.

Acts on the currently selected account; call get_account if unsure.

posts.description: The post bodies, exactly as they would be sent. Link detection runs on this text, so paste the real thing. Omit when pricing AI work on its own.

immediate.description: True to price publishing now rather than scheduling. Publishing now is cheaper.

ai_actions.description: Price AI work too. Only counts when the user has no API key of their own, with one, AI is free and quotes 0.

account_ids.description: Which connected accounts to post to, by id from get_account. Omit to use the key’s own group if it has one, else the user’s default group. Use this OR group, never both. An id the key does not own -- or that exists but is outside the key’s group -- fails the whole call, nothing is silently dropped.

group.description: Post to a named group of accounts, e.g. "Business". Groups are listed by get_account. If this key is itself scoped to a group, that is the only name it can pass here. Use this OR account_ids, never both.

instructions:
No Kunopilot account is configured yet.
Create an API key at https://bskycopilot.com/settings/, then either:
  - run: npx kunopilot-mcp@latest add-account --key bskc_...
  - or set KUNOPILOT_API_KEY for a single account
Then restart this MCP server.

Analytics responses carry a `sample` block and sometimes `warnings`. Read them.
sample.truncated means the answer came from part of the account, not all of it.
say so when you report a conclusion. confidence: none or low means the finding is
not distinguishable from noise; do not present it as fact.
We store at most 200 posts per account. sync_posts with depth: "full" reaches that
limit; list_live_posts reads past it without storing.

Prefer get_suggestion_prompt and get_rewrite_prompt over generate_suggestions
and rewrite_post. The prompt tools return the real prompt with the account's
own posts already in it, cost the user nothing, and you can run them yourself.
The generating tools spend the user's own Anthropic or OpenAI credit.

Never call publish_draft without asking the user first. It posts publicly and
cannot be undone, and it requires you to name the account as confirmation.
